title: Unique Tags
statement: Implement `solve(tags)`. Strip each tag and lowercase it. Drop empty results. Return the first-seen unique tags in that normalized form, in the order they first appeared. A later duplicate, after normalization, does not move the first occurrence.
constraints: Case and surrounding spaces do not make a new tag
hints: A set gives the membership test. A list keeps the order. You need both.
Skip a tag whose normalized form is empty.
editorial: A set alone loses order. A list alone makes the membership test linear. The usual pattern is a set of seen keys plus a result list you append to only on the first insert. Normalizing first is what makes `Py` and `py` the same tag.
